turnaround_reason: CNXC, a global CX/BPO outsourcer, has been de-rated to a rock-bottom multiple (forward P/E ~2.4, P/B 0.65, EV/EBITDA 5.5) on fears that generative AI structurally erodes its contact-center core. The bull case is that it is dramatically oversold relative to still-strong free cash flow and an emerging AI-services pivot.
bullish_points: Deep value on every metric: forward P/E ~2.4, EV/revenue 0.70, P/B 0.65, EV/EBITDA 5.5, with robust FCF (~$775M TTM)
AI pivot showing traction: iX Suite contract signings reportedly up 400% YoY — evidence it can sell AI rather than only be disrupted by it
CEO and CFO made open-market purchases in 2026 ($21-28 range), signaling insider conviction near the lows
Analyst consensus still 'buy' with mean target $36.25 vs $29 quote; positive 30-day momentum (+12%)
bearish_points: Core secular threat is genuine: AI is compressing traditional seat-based outsourcing; Q2 stock fell ~22% on a full-year guidance cut driven by client offshoring and weak demand
Heavy leverage: $5.5B debt, D/E ~204, EV $7B — magnifies any revenue erosion
Major holder Groupe Bruxelles Lambert sold 6M shares (~$133M) in Apr 2026 — a large overhang that dwarfs the small insider buys
GAAP net margin negative (profit margin -13%); high short interest (~18% of float)
catalyst: Q3 FY2026 earnings — proof that guidance has stabilized and AI/iX Suite revenue is offsetting legacy erosion
suggested_trade: Small starter spot only, ahead of or into the 9/29 print; the cheapness is real but the AI disruption is a live secular risk. Size for a value trap.
key_risk: AI-driven revenue erosion accelerates and another guidance cut confirms the business is structurally shrinking, turning the low multiple into a value trap
would_skip_if: You believe generative AI permanently impairs seat-based BPO economics, or you want to avoid a highly levered name with a large selling anchor holder
